newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-PUMAS SEEK HELP FROM IRB.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PUMAS SEEK HELP FROM IRB.

text.p: Argentina headed for home on Sunday with a plea to the International Rugby Board (IRB) to help them build on their unlucky 20-18 defeat to England at Twickenham.
The Pumas lost to a late English try claimed by stand-in captain Jason Leonard, confirming they have the talent to bother the best sides in the world.

Coach Jose Luis Imhoff rated the performance alongside the promising displays against France and Canada this year, but is still desperate to welcome key foreign-based players such as Federico Mendez and Patricio Noriega back into the fold.
The immensely strong Noriega is carving out a new career in Australia and Imhoff wants the IRB to tighten the eligibility rules which allow players to represent two different countries.
"Argentina is going to ask the International Board to make a decision that once a rugby player plays in an international shirt, he can't wear another one," said Imhoff.
"It can't be that a player can have two or even three jerseys in his life. Rugby is a sport of free men, but we must know how to accept the rules."
Imhoff's point was underlined by the sight of Argentine-born Diego Dominguez scoring 17 points in Italy's 29-22 defeat by Scotland on Saturday.

The Argentine Rugby Union have already relaxed their ban on foreign-based players playing for the national side, and there appears to be an increasing desire to ensure the Pumas are not trampled underfoot in the new professional era.
"I think Argentine rugby is changing, especially in our heads," said captain Lisandro Arbizu, proud of the way his side bounced back from their two heavy home defeats to South Africa.
"There has been more communication between officials and players on this tour which is a step forward. We have reached a point where we must change."
The Pumas, beaten 51-0 at Twickenham in 1990, will not have to wait too long for another crack at England, who are due to tour Argentina next year.
The trip clashes with the British Isles tour to South Africa which will ensure a weakened England side, although few members of the home side enhanced their Lions chances on Saturday.
Non-playing captain Phil de Glanville admitted England had been "well below-par" and coach Jack Rowell conceded that new faces would be seriously considered for the Five Nations in the New Year.
Fly-half Mike Catt is under particular scrutiny despite kicking five penalties, but Rowell suggested England's critics should be more patient.
"We won, didn't we? As Ruud Gullit said recently, you can't always play the beautiful game."
